title: ECNet-guided selection of higher-order TEM-1 variants
summary: ECNet integrated evolutionary context with learned sequence representations to prioritize previously untested higher-order TEM-1 variants. The authors constructed and measured 37 selected variants under ampicillin selection, using relative resistance as an enzyme-fitness proxy. The assays do not imply clinical treatment outcomes, and the reported group of 37 should not be read as showing that every variant improved.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature indexed article and author-hosted full text; official bioRxiv API checked and identified the previously associated preprint DOI as a different paper.

evidence.tested: Thirty-seven previously untested higher-order TEM-1 variants selected with ECNet were constructed and experimentally measured under ampicillin selection against wild-type and study controls. The study uses relative resistance as an enzyme-fitness proxy.
evidence.unknown: The bounded entry does not imply that all 37 variants improved equally, does not establish clinical outcomes, and makes no claim of independent sequence novelty beyond the authors’ screened literature.
evidence.ai_role: ECNet integrated evolutionary context and a learned representation to prioritize higher-order TEM-1 variants for experimental construction and ampicillin-selection measurements.
